headline: Scientists Revive Pig Kidneys After Year in Deep Freeze
meta_description: Researchers successfully revived pig kidneys that had been frozen for a year, opening new possibilities for organ transplantation.
summary_short: In a breakthrough for transplant medicine, scientists have successfully revived pig kidneys after one year of frozen storage—a development that could transform how organ…
body:
Scientists have successfully revived pig kidneys that had been frozen for a year, marking a significant step forward in organ preservation technology.

The achievement suggests that organs no longer need to be used immediately after harvest. If the technique can be refined and applied to human organs, it could fundamentally change transplant logistics—allowing organs to be stored longer, transported farther, and matched more carefully to waiting patients.

This breakthrough comes from work submitted by natural scientists exploring cryopreservation methods. The ability to thaw and restore organ function after extended frozen storage addresses one of transplantation's most pressing challenges: the narrow window currently available to surgeons and the geographic limitations that often waste viable organs.
